web/execution/service.py:R5:_merge_autho: This is an offensive assertion of an ELSPETH-OWNED invariant that RAISES, not a Tier-3 defensive shape probe, and it is the ADR-032 treatment of a broken owned invariant: crash, do not repair. `diagnostics` is the return value of `compute_proof_diagnostics` (web/composer/tools/generation.py), first-party code — but its declared type is `list[Mapping[str, Any]]`, so every value read out of one diagnostic is statically `Any`. `evidence = diagnostic["evidence_locator"]` followed by `if not isinstance(evidence, Mapping): raise RuntimeError("proof diagnostic evidence_locator must be a mapping")` therefore does two jobs at once. First, it fails the authoritative preflight loudly if the proof producer ever emits a non-mapping evidence_locator — the sole outcome of a failed check is the RuntimeError; nothing is defaulted, coerced, or skipped, and no `.get()` or `or {}` softens it. Second, it is the only narrowing that lets `_proof_component_type(code, evidence)` receive the value under its declared `Mapping[str, Any]` parameter, so deleting the guard would require a `cast`, converting a real crash into a silent mis-parse of the operator-facing blocking-diagnostic projection. `Mapping` (the ABC) rather than the house `type(x) is dict` idiom is required because the producer's own declared element type is `Mapping[str, Any]`: an exact-`dict` test would reject a `MappingProxyType` the producer is free to return and would turn a valid diagnostic into a spurious RuntimeError. Drift that gave `compute_proof_diagnostics` an owned typed return, or that replaced the raise with an abstain, would invalidate this justification.
web/execution/service.py:R5:_operator_ex: `isinstance(exc, PydanticValidationError)` is subclass-inclusive ON PURPOSE and is the redaction control itself, not a probe of parsed data. `exc` is an arbitrary in-flight exception from the run's failure path (first-party control flow, not Tier-3 input); the branch selects the ONLY safe rendering for a pydantic `ValidationError`, whose `str()` interleaves a raw `input_value=...` fragment per error — the config/row payload the audit trail deliberately keeps out of `runs.error`. The function's own docstring records why: `scrub_text_for_audit` replaces candidate-secret PATTERNS only, so an arbitrary payload sails through the scrubber intact, and the safe rendering is instead built from `_schema_contract_violation_errors` (dotted `loc` plus the pydantic error `type`, never the input). Converting to the house exact-type idiom `type(exc) is PydanticValidationError` is a SECURITY REGRESSION rather than a style change: a `ValidationError` subclass — pydantic's own or a library's — would fall through to `_scrubbed_exception_message` and re-open exactly the leak this branch exists to close. The docstring already states this commitment ("`isinstance` — not the exact-type check the schema-contract slog uses for its closed taxonomy — so a ValidationError subclass cannot reintroduce the leak"). web/execution/service.py:R6:ExecutionSer: R6 flags `try: parsed_blob_id = UUID(raw_blob_id) / except ValueError: continue` as a silent swallow. `raw_blob_id` is `source.options["blob_ref"]`, a Tier-3 composer/planner-authored option value, and `ValueError` is how `uuid.UUID` reports 'this string is not a UUID' — the negative answer to a question, not a fault to propagate. This handler is NOT the gate that protects execution. A malformed `blob_ref` is rejected before a run row exists at all, by `MalformedBlobRefError` on the execute path — pinned by tests/unit/web/execution/test_service.py::TestBlobRefPreValidation::test_malformed_blob_ref_raises_before_run_creation, which additionally asserts `create_run()` is never called. What this loop builds is `expected_paths_by_blob_id`, the census of blob ids whose custody the authoritative proof may resolve, and the named control that makes an omission from that census SAFE is `_unresolved`, the closure defined immediately below in the same function: `_resolve` routes any blob id absent from the census through `_unresolved`, which returns a blocking `UnresolvedClaimedProofBlob` for every retained sentinel claim in `claimed_sentinel_blob_ids` and `None` otherwise. The abstain is therefore strictly fail-closed — it can only withhold a proof pass, never fabricate one. Re-raising here would abort the entire authoritative preflight on one malformed authored option instead of blocking the single pipeline that carries it. R6 is outside the {R1,R5} set any `@trust_boundary` can suppress, so no decorator can carry this site.

`except BlobNotFoundError: return None` RECORDS an absence rather than hiding a fault, and the absence is converted into a visible BLOCKING outcome by a named control. `_blob_get_metadata` is the sync metadata lookup handed to `validate_pipeline(blob_get_metadata=...)`; its declared return type is `BlobRecord | None` and `None` is its documented 'no such blob' answer. The control chain is: `_validate_blob_content_refs_sync` (elspeth/core/blobs_inline.py) omits any ref whose lookup returned `None` from `records_by_blob_id`; `_evaluate_blob_content_ref_metadata` then appends that ref to its `missing` list; `_metadata_evaluation_validation_violations` turns each into a `BlobInlineValidationViolation`; and `materialize_validation_yaml` (web/execution/_validation_materialization.py) renders those as a FAILED `blob_inline_refs` ValidationCheck with readiness code `blob_inline_refs`. The run is BLOCKED, not passed — nothing is fabricated and no default value substitutes for the missing record. The catch is a single typed exception; every other blob-store failure (BlobStateError, SQLAlchemyError, integrity errors) propagates and aborts validation, and the sibling `record.session_id != session_id` arm returns None for the same 'treat another session's blob exactly as missing' IDOR contract. The conversion was MEASURED, not assumed — replacing this line with `type(materialized_state) is InterpretationReviewPending` and running mypy produces `error: Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type "CompositionState | InterpretationReviewPending", variable has type "CompositionState")` at the assignment immediately below the branch. The check is load-bearing typing over an owned sum type, not runtime paranoia. Drift that made this union open, or that stopped consuming the non-sentinel arm as a `CompositionState`, would invalidate this justification.

This is the prescribed Tier-3 boundary shape check, and the choice of `Mapping` over the house `type(x) is dict` idiom is REQUIRED — narrowing it would be a security regression, not a style change. `node.options` is user/composer-authored composition state, so `provider_config = node.options["provider_config"]` is an arbitrary authored value and must be shape-checked before it is subscripted. The loop it guards is the defence-in-depth confinement of nested RAG `persist_directory` writes to the session's allowed sink directories, which exists precisely because `/execute` does not require `/validate` first. `NodeSpec.__post_init__` calls `freeze_fields(self, "options")`, and `deep_freeze` renders every nested mapping as `MappingProxyType`: measured, `type(deep_freeze({'provider_config': {...}})['provider_config'])` is `mappingproxy`, for which `type(x) is dict` is False. An exact-type test would therefore `continue` past EVERY frozen node and silently disable this allowlist for the normal case. The `continue` on a genuine non-mapping is the correct polarity: a non-mapping `provider_config` carries no nested path key to confine, and plugin option validation rejects it downstream; a mapping that DOES carry a path key is resolved and raises `PathAllowlistViolationError` on escape. web/execution/service.py:R6:ExecutionSer: Nothing is swallowed. This handler is nested INSIDE the outer setup-failure handler and is followed, at the same indentation as its own `try`, by a bare `raise` that re-raises the ORIGINAL setup exception — so the primary failure always reaches the caller and the run's outcome is never misreported as success. The handler's only job is to stop a failed best-effort `update_run_status(run_id, status="failed", ...)` from REPLACING the real fault with a cleanup fault; that status write exists so a setup failure does not leave a pending run permanently blocking the session's one-active-run constraint. The absence is not silent either: the named control is the structured `slog.error("run_cleanup_status_update_failed", ...)` emitted in the handler, carrying `run_id`, `original_exc_class` and `cleanup_exc_class`. The catch tuple is narrow by design — `SQLAlchemyError` covers every DB-layer failure mode and `OSError` the filesystem-adjacent ones SQLite can surface before SQLAlchemy wraps them, while programmer bugs from our own service code (`AttributeError`, `TypeError`, `KeyError`) are deliberately OUTSIDE the tuple and propagate, because a cleanup path masking a programmer bug is the silent-wrong-result pattern this repository forbids. `exc_class` only and never `str(cleanup_err)`, because SQLAlchemyError's `str()` expands to `[SQL: ...] [parameters: ...]` and can carry DB URLs or credentials.
